## Introduction
This report is to present an analysis of crimes committed in Western Africa.

![Bullet on the floor](https://images.pexels.com/photos/34590928/pexels-photo-34590928.jpeg){width=50%}


To approach the analysis, we make use of base R functions and `dplyr` package for added analysis. The package is loaded using the `library()` function.

```{r}
#| label: load-pkgs
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
```

Firstly we create objects of the crime data
```{r}
#|label: create-objects 

country <- c(rep("Nigeria", 3), "Cameroon", rep("Nigeria", 3), 
  "Cameroon", rep("Nigeria", 8), "Cameroon", rep("Nigeria", 3))
country
```


```{r}
length(country)
unique(country)
```

City preview

```{r}
city <- c("Maiduguri", "Unknown", "Kano", "Bamenda", "Port Harcourt",
          "Potiskum", "Damaturu", "Unknown", "Jos", "Lagos", "Gombe", "Kaduna",
          "Logo district", "Konduga", "Warri", "Bama", "Buea", "Buni Yadi",
          "Damboa", "Gamboru"
          )
city
```

This is a preview of the crime committed
```{r}
n_crime <- c(488, 225, 130, 87, 76, 65, 63, 55, 51, 46, 42, 38, 37, 36, 35, 32,
             31, 30, 30, 29)
n_crime
```

## Data Structure and type
To ensure proper analysis we have to investigate if the data are the right types and have the right structure.

```{r}
typeof(country)
typeof(city)
typeof(n_crime)
```

The data types are of expected, with `typeof()` exposing that `country` and `city`, are both `r typeof(country)`.


```{r}
## Data Structure
str(country)
str(city)
str(n_crime)
```
The number of elements in the object `country` is `r length(n_crime)` and this is the same for `city` and `n_crime`.

## Data analysis

The total number of crime committed is `r sum(n_crime)`. It would be nice to have indepth analysis about the countries and the crimes committed there. It is important to aggregate this data and change its structure to a `data.frame` to ensure smooth analysis.

```{r}
crime_tbl <- data.frame(
  country,
  city,
  n_crime
)

crime_tbl |> head()
```

Next, we separate regions according to the level of crime from high to low.
```{r}
crime_tbl$crime_rate <- ifelse(
  test = crime_tbl$n_crime >= 400,
  yes = "High",
  no = ifelse(
    test = crime_tbl$n_crime >= 100,
    yes = "Medium",
    no = "Low"
  )
)

crime_tbl |> 
  head() |> 
  knitr::kable()
```
The total number of crime commited in each region is given below.

```{r}
# Total number of crime and its average per country

aggregate(crime_tbl$n_crime, by = list(country = country), FUN = "sum")
```

Alternatively, we could this using `dplyr` and we can get the average crime per region in the process of getting the total.
```{r}
crime_tbl |> 
  summarize(
    .by = country,
    total_crime = sum(n_crime),
    average_number_of_crime = mean(n_crime)
  )|> 
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
crime_tbl |> 
  summarize(
    .by = country,
    total_crime = sum(n_crime),
    average_number_of_crime = mean(n_crime)
  )
```



The country with the highest crime is given below.
```{r}
crime_tbl |> 
  summarize(
    .by = country,
    total_crime = sum(n_crime)
  ) |> 
  top_n(n = 1, wt = total_crime) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```
